stocks.note: Numbers as of market close on June 16th.
stocks.news:
Stocks were mixed — the S&P 500 slipped 0.57% and the NASDAQ fell 1.15% as chip names pulled back, while the DOW added 0.64%. The Fed meets today, with a rate decision due this afternoon.

The big theme is AI spending. Microsoft (MSFT -1.48%) is reportedly in talks to rent about $3 billion of computing power from rival Oracle (ORCL -2.24%) — a cloud giant renting cloud — because AI is eating up capacity faster than it can build, and Microsoft says it will stay short on capacity into mid-2026. The hyperscalers are pouring record sums into data centers and chips: Amazon, Microsoft, Google, and Meta are each projected to spend roughly $145–200 billion on AI this year (see the chart below).

Chips are the bottleneck. Nvidia (NVDA -2.37%) CEO Jensen Huang asked Korea's SK Hynix to make more memory chips at Taiwan's biggest tech show this month, while U.S. memory maker Micron (MU -6.18%) — up more than 250% this year — gave back some of its run.

Dealmaking stayed hot: SpaceX (SPCX +4.83%), fresh off the biggest IPO in history, said it will buy four-year-old AI coding startup Cursor for $60 billion to feed its Grok AI; and GM (GM -1.86%) struck a deal with defense giant Lockheed Martin (LMT +1.05%) to scale U.S. munitions manufacturing — Lockheed spending $9 billion through 2030 and GM putting $7 billion into U.S. R&D.

economy.note: 10-Year as of June 16th (Fed decision due today); gold, silver & Brent are live spot, June 17th (Trading Economics).
economy.commentary:
Rates and metals were steady-to-firm ahead of today's Fed decision. The 10-year Treasury held near 4.47%, gold edged up to about $4,352 (+0.47%), and silver firmed to $70.42 (+0.57%) — still one of 2026's standout performers, up roughly 100% year-to-date. Brent crude sits around $79–80, a touch higher on the day but down about 4% on the week and nearly 29% over the past month: the U.S. and Iran reached a framework to end their war that could put Iranian oil back on the market and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, with a deal possibly signed as early as Friday.

For housing, the supply picture is flashing caution. Builders broke ground on 40% fewer apartment buildings in May than the month before, and permits for new single-family homes also fell month over month. With higher prices pressuring both buyers and renters, fewer sales and lease signings are pushing builders to pause projects — the opposite of what an under-supplied market needs.

crypto.note: Numbers as of 4:00 PM ET, June 16th.
crypto.commentary:
Crypto pulled back across the board: Bitcoin at $64,625 (-1.51%), Ether at $1,764 (-1.42%), and XRP at $1.19 (-2.15%). The bigger story is where crypto and traditional markets are merging — Coinbase (COIN -0.21%) is launching tokenized U.S. stocks, backed one-for-one by real shares and paying dividends automatically, pitched as real ownership with "no derivatives, no IOUs" and 24/7 trading. The catch: it starts outside the U.S., so American users wait on regulators while Kraken and Robinhood (HOOD -1.44%) already offer their own versions.

Overseas, Binance is preparing to exit the European Union after Greece signaled it may cancel the platform's license — and because one EU license normally covers all 27 countries, a single rejection can shut the whole bloc. Rivals Coinbase and Kraken could scoop up the users Binance loses.

real_estate.homebuilder: Mortgage Rates Ease To 6.54% As Builders Pull Back — Apartment Starts Drop 40% In May; The East Bay Board Slips To 2,858 Active On 237 New And 210 Closed
real_estate.commentary:
The 30-year fixed eased to 6.54% and the 15-year to 6.11% — a touch lower than last week — though all eyes are on the Fed's rate decision later today.

Nationally, the supply picture is the worry. Builders broke ground on 40% fewer apartment buildings in May than the month before, and permits for new single-family homes also fell month over month. With higher prices pressuring both buyers and renters, fewer sales and lease signings are pushing builders to pause projects — which only deepens the long-run shortage that keeps that crucial first rung out of reach for many.

Locally, the East Bay board slipped to 2,858 active (down 24 from yesterday), with 237 new listings against 210 closings. Oakland again led the board with 65 new on 754 active; Fremont added 24 new on 356 active.

New-listing flow eased to 237 (down 11 from yesterday's 248), led by Oakland (65), Dublin (27), Livermore (26), Fremont (24), and San Ramon (22). Closings came in at 210.

For agents: the national mood is cautious — builders are breaking less ground and pulling permits as affordability bites — but locally the board is steady at 2,858 active with a healthy 237 new listings still coming in. Well-priced, well-presented homes that sell inside about four weeks continue to win. Coach sellers to price right and show well; remind buyers that slightly softer rates give them a little more room to negotiate.
